I'm interested in what all of you used and what you like when it comes to your keyboards, mice etc. Preferably what you actually have experience using. I'm in the middle of a build and I have been out of the loop on all the good, bad, and ugly when it comes to that stuff.
Gaming peripherals: What do you use, what have you used and what are your opinions on them?

Mouse: Logitech G600 - 3 fewer thumb buttons than the Razer Naga, but infinitely better build quality.

Gamepad: Xbox 360 (wired).

Joystick: Thrustmaster T-Flight HOTAS X. Not exactly top of the line, but feels solid and has great responsiveness. Unfortunately, it can't play the damned escort missions for me.

Keyboard: IBM Model M, circa 1991. Kind of crap for gaming, but no damn Windows keys, and the clicky.

Add-on: Nostromo N52 - a "left hand keyboard" peripheral to make up for the Model M. Doesn't get much use now that I have the G600 to program macros into.

Also a user of the G600. I picked it up for a really good deal ($30 on sale) about a year ago now. Have been using it almost everyday. For the first few months I setup a whole bunch of macros and shortcuts, but of late I have found myself not using them anymore. This is partly due to me switching operating systems fairly regularly. The build quality is great and it has gone through a bashing with the only visible wear being the scratched bottom surface and the fraying fabric cable, all of aren't hindering performance. My opinion is that if you have a use for the buttons, and you don't mind using a chunky (yet comfortable and smooth) piece of tech than this is for you. Otherwise I would suggest going with a slimmer more simple mouse. This mouse worked for me and I couldn't ask for more from it.

Keyboard: Doesn't really matter what keyboard you get, you can get rubber dome, mechanical, and a few other, but those two are the most popular. Under 50 dollars= rubber dome. More than 50= you can get a pretty decent mechanical. Mouse is one of the main important, as depending on the game (give fps for example) can make a difference in comfort, performance, and overall asthetics. This would be best if you go to you local store and try out the mouses their, then read online and see the info and reviews. Monitor: Depending on the budget, you can get one on sale, this monitor has the perfect size in my opinion and won't break the bank. It also has 1ms response time and great colors:monitor Headset: Logitech G930 Wireless This is refurbished but with the money you save, you can get a warranty for 7 bucks. Last but not least, you can a mousepad like the steelseries ones for 9 dollars.

Currently using:

  • Logitech G502
  • Ducky Shine 3 MX blue
  • wired XBox 360 gamepad
  • Pro Flight X-55 Rhino H.O.T.A.S.

The G502 is definitely the best mouse I have ever used. No complaints about anything in hardware or software. Rather expensive though.
Same goes for the Shine 3, very good hardware quality but not cheap.
The 360 gamepad lays good in my hands and has perfect driver support on Windows.
I am using the X-55 mostly for Elite Dangerous. Again, it is rather expensive and if you are looking to get started with a HOTAS, you should go for the Thrustmaster T.Flight Hotas X.

Have used:

  • Razer Diamondback
  • Razer Copperhead
  • Logitech G11
  • Thrustmaster T.Flight Hotas X

The Diamondback and Copperhead are sadly not produced anymore and I had a long drought without any mouse really fitting my hand until the G502 came out.
Same for the G11, has not been made for years. The G11 and G15 are as good as rubberdome keyboards will ever get, but with the wide range of keyboards with cherry switches that is available at the moment this is not really a concern.
The Thrustmaster T.Flight Hotas X is the perfect entry level HOTAS. Very high build quality, precise and smooth to use.

Conclusion:

I would not go near any Razer product these days as they have gone weird on their drivers and their quality has greatly suffered.
For quality mice, it is Logitech all the way.
For keyboards it really depends on what you want. If you are fine with a rubberdome one, every cheap one will do the job. I would really consider a mechanical one though, that clicky feeling is unmatched. Brand wise, there are not really any bad ones. Still, more money will buy you better stuff.
Don't go cheap on gamepads. The cheap ones suck. Go for a 360/xbone or a PS3/4 one. They work perfectly fine and are build well. Also, avoid the wireless 360 pad. The battery pack is clunky and drains way to fast, even with good batteries.

My setup is:

  • Mouse: Steelseries Kana v2 - I like it, but I had to apply the LOD tape fix to get it how I like it.
  • Keyboard: Corsair K90 w/ Cherry MX Red keys - Maybe a bit overkill for my needs, I like the macro keys but rarely use them.
  • Gamepad: Xbox 360 wireless, Wiimotes/Nunchuks or Wii u Pro controller, depending what I'm playing. If you have to get one gamepad, Xbox 360 or Xbone is what you should be purchasing.
  • Keypad: Razer Nostromo if I'm playing a FPS or moba on the laptop or desktop from my couch/bed. I really like this but it's far from essential, I also use a kinzu v2 mouse when laptop gaming.

As a new commer to the master race I got a logitech g502. The build quality of the mouse itself is great but the wire needs some work. I use a ROG laptop so i didn't buy a new keyboard. The keyboard on the laptop is very nice and i have run into no problems.

Personally, this is me:

Keyboard: Vortex POK3R with Cherry MX Red switches. I love this. It feels like quality. It's small and that's not to everyone's tastes, but coming from a Logitech K400r I'm fine with it. This also gives more room for a bigger mousepad, which I'll talk about later.

Mouse: Steelseries Rival. I was going to buy a Logitech G502, but I got to try it in store and it felt bad in my hand :( So I took a chance and bought the Rival because it looked comfy to me, used by many people and had good reviews. No regrets. RGB lighting is very pretty, too. DPI switcher is useless so don't use it. I use the back/forward buttons WAY more than I thought I would.

Mousepad: Mionix Sargas 400/Glorious PC Gaming Race Large. I prefer the former, and I got it for free which was nice (I'm probably not allowed to say why). Performance wise the Mionix feels fricking fantastic with my mouse. PC Gaming Race anti-fray is very good, and the Mionix doesn't have that, and is already showing signs of wear just a month or so after getting it :( I switch between these.

Headset: Beyerdynamic MMX1. Audio is great. Microphone is quite good too according to friends but it picks up a lot of background noise, unfortunately. I will probably be "upgrading" to a Beyerdynamic DT770 PRO with a V-Moda Boompro.

Mouse is a Mionix Naos 5000. Love it for its (once) unique shape - although another brand called "Func" seem to have copied their design exactly. Or maybe Mionix copied Func? Either way, it's a beautiful shape worth copying, crazy comfortable, and I'm a palm gripper so it works great for me.

Keyboard is a Corsair K70, MX Red switches. Love that thing. I would like to try more mechanical keyboards though, get some better switch variety under my belt. I'd love to try Topre switches. Money though.

I use a DS3 when I want to use a gamepad. Prefer its sticks over the Xbox 360's controller - greater range and less stiff. Not the best body shape though, if I could have the DS3's internals inside the shell of an Xbox 360 controller that'd be ideal.

Mice:

  • Microsoft Compact Optical Mouse: This was my first mouse, I used it for several years. It's nothing special, but got the job done. Scroll wheel is a bit wishy washy.

  • Logitech M305: I really liked this one, because I finally didn't have to deal with a cord. It is accurate, not too heavy and I liked the left and right click of the scroll wheel. The scroll wheel is very hard to click, though, and you often accidentally click one of the side buttons while pressing it down.

  • Logitech G700: It's pretty good. I mainly bought it because of the many buttons and the free-scroll feature. I've never really gotten used to the way it handles, though. It's quite heavy and since the right side is curved down, it's hard to get a grip on it when you want to lift it. And I'm the type of guy that lifts the mouse often.

  • Logitech G700s: I got that as an RMA. It has a couple improvements over the original G700, but I had the same problems with it since it's basically just a refresh.

  • Logitech G502 Proteus Core: This is what I'm currently using. I really like it even though it's not wireless. It's very accurate, not too heavy and easy to lift and has enough buttons for my needs and also the really cool free-scroll feature that I've come to really love.

Keyboards:

  • Some old Fujitsu Siemens keyboard: Nothing special, did its job.

  • Logitech G510: Got it because of all those macro buttons, the screen and the RGB lighting. I expected a bit higher quality, but it was a very nice first step into gaming keyboards.

  • Corsair K95: I wanted a mechanical keyboard, but didn't want to sacrifice the features of my G510. The K95 had the main feature I was looking for, the 15 macro buttons, but I had to compromise the screen and RGB lighting. Other than that, I really enjoyed the clicky clacks and was very happy with it until the LED's started dying.

  • Corsair K95 RGB: This is what I'm currently using. Luckily this one got released when the LED's of my K95 started dying, so I returned the K95 and got the K95 RGB with that fancy lighting. I'm very happy with it.

Headsets/phones:

  • Cheap dollar-store headset: I don't know what it's called, it had a vibrating feature whenever there was intense base, which was pretty cool. I was pretty happy with it, but looking back, it didn't have great sound, but for what it's worth, it was pretty good.

  • Microsoft LifeChat LX-3000: Better sound quality, but was less comfortable. I was pretty happy with it, though, until the microphone got a slack joint.

  • Logitech G35: I initially had some sound quality issues due to bad driver software, but they got fixed. It has decent sound quality for both mic and speakers and good build quality. I really loved the control buttons on the speaker cup.

  • beyerdynamic DT770 PRO 250Ohm: This is what I'm currently using. I love these headphones. Awesome sound quality and comfortable to wear. Well, at least the ear cushions. Coming from the broad and soft headband cushion of the G35, the headband cushion was rather uncomfortable for me, so I modded it to hold one of the three G35 cushions (The G35 has exchangable cushions held in place by velcro). I have it plugged into a Schiit-Stack, Magni/Modi.

Other:

I also have a Saitek X-55 Rhino HOTAS. Even though it's 99% plastic, it has an awesome build quality, is accurate and has tons of buttons and switches to bind. I really enjoy playing Elite: Dangerous with it.
From what I've heard about those X-55s it sounds like you got lucky.

Well, I did have the power-loss issue on the throttle at first. I had it plugged into a USB 3.0 port. I fixed it by plugging it into a USB 2 port which is kinda counterintuitive. Other than that I had absolutely no trouble with it.

Mouse: Logitech G502 proteus. This is a mouse that I took a while to convince myself to purchase. It is expensive, but it has excellent build quality, with top notch everything with only a few exceptions. First, The scroll wheel click is mushy, and I've read that it is not an Omron switch, but some lesser switch, (All the rest in the mouse are Omron), and the side scrolling is iffy at best. But that is pretty much it for the problems. The wheel more than makes up for it for me by having one of those momentum spinny jigs.

I used to use a Razer Taipan. This is great for people who want a high DPI laser sensor that isn't awful, (though its not much cheaper than the G502). I got rid of it because it was ambidextrous and I wanted more ergonomics.

Mousepad: I have a Razer Manticor, a discontinued hard metal mouse pad that's okay. I'd recommend a hybrid if you want the best, or just a normal non-gaming cheapo if you want the cheapest.

Keyboard: I use a Daskeyboard 4 Ultimate, MX blues. I love my clicky blues, and its a joy to clickity clack away. I chose the keyboard because it's no frills and very stylish, no lights, and blank keycaps to force me to learn touch-typing, (which worked but it took longer than I would have guessed). Also it has a built in USB 3 hub, and a lot of other subtle features. This one is a big recommendation from me.

I also have a Duckly shine at work, (MX browns). Its a 60% keyboard which is great for space saving efforts but I do miss the arrow keys from time to time. I'd probably say there's nothing bad about it, it's as advertised but if you weren't already thinking about getting it, there are other choices...

Headphones: I currently own the Corsair 2100. It's surprising how many things I can nitpick on this thing, no battery indicator, no low battery warning, no intentional or obvious "on" noise, (though there is static). But it is wireless and I was surprised how much I liked that once I got it.

I used to own the Logitech G35 and honestly, as I remember it, that headset was superior in every way. It sounded better, it had a mute button for your microphone, (handy for not sneezing in your chat partner's ear). It looked a little goofier though, so if that matters to you... I ditched these because the leather on the ear cups started peeling off and I couldn't find any replacements.

My next headphones will be whatever wireless headphones Logitech has out when these ones break.

Controller: I currenly own an XBONE controller. It's okay. Controllers can be expensive so I guess for the price this one is pretty good considering its the golden standard for a lot of games so a lot support it, so it's got that going for it.

Razer Naga molten edition MMO Mouse, can't live without it since first I got it, I even had to fixt it twice already for difference problems, I'm not letting go.

Keypad Logitech G13, you would be surprising how amazing that controller is for not just MMO games but also for air combat games like Elite Dangerous, seriously I don't need a joystyck.

For keyboard, Razer black widow, I prefer Razer keyboards because of the ability to macro any key, unlike Logitech keyboards, but Logitech keypad is better than Razer keypad imo.

For sounds Logitech G930, I love that wireless headset.

Mouse: Logitech M510. Wireless, precise, and has a couple extra buttons on the thumb.

Keyboard: Logitech K200. Simple, cheap, effective. I'm looking to upgrade to a mechanical keyboard, but this one has lasted for a good few years.

Other controllers:

Afterglow Xbox gamepad. Nice wired pad, just as good quality as standard Xbox 360 controllers.

Logitech G13 gamepad: Not used as often as the other controllers, but gives me extra buttons for control-heavy games like Arma and Star Citizen.

CH Fighterstick and Pro Throttle: This HOTAS setup is on the pricy side, but goddamn is it worth it. The stick and throttle are made of pure nintendium, since CH is primarily an industrial control company. They're perfect for flying in games like Arma and Star Citizen.
Mouse - Steelseries rival, has a great senor and feel awesome in the hand ( ͡~ ͜ʖ ͡°) Keyboard - CM Storm QF TK - its aight for the price. Mouse pad - MM200, idk what to say.
